content: The Federation of Chiropractic Licensing Boards (FCLB) was officially established in 1926, although it operated under different names in its early years. The primary mission of the FCLB is to uphold high and consistent standards in chiropractic licensure, regulation, discipline, and education. The FCLB hosts an annual conference and district meetings, which serve as platforms for member boards to exchange ideas and perspectives. These gatherings also facilitate the unified adoption of resolutions aimed at safeguarding the profession’s regulatory and examination standards, ultimately ensuring the protection of the public. The FCLB maintains a database known as CIN-BAD (Chiropractic Information Network Board Action Database). This resource provides member boards and other subscribers with access to information about licensed chiropractors in the United States, Canada, and Australia. The CIN-BAD database is continually expanding and has become an increasingly valuable tool for regulatory boards, chiropractic colleges, managed care providers, law enforcement agencies, and the general public. The FCLB’s membership includes boards that have the authority to license or regulate chiropractic practice in the states, provinces, commonwealths, and territories of the United States, Canada, Australia, Mexico, and other countries. Current members of regulatory boards, as well as those who have served on such boards within the past five years, are eligible to participate as Fellows in FCLB activities. These activities include holding office or serving on standing committees. Individuals who have ever served on a chiropractic regulatory board are designated as Honorary Fellows and are entitled to attend the annual business meeting. The FCLB collaborates closely with sister organizations, such as the National Board of Chiropractic Examiners and the Council on Chiropractic Education, due to their shared mission of protecting the public.
